messages.subject: old seeds
messages.text:
Hello,
 I purchased a few packs of seeds from Lasclay last year. I misplace the envelope they came in, only recently found it.
 
 Is there any way to grow milkweed from these seeds, or am I out of luck?
 
 Please advise.
 
 Regards,
 
 Larry Blankemeyer
 Richboro, PA

messages.subject: Re: old seeds
messages.text:
Hi Larry,

Good news: milkweed seeds are quite resilient, and seeds stored for a year in an envelope still have a solid chance of germinating, especially if they were kept somewhere reasonably cool and dry.

The key thing at this point in the season is stratification. Since you're planting in spring/summer rather than fall, the seeds need a cold treatment first to break their dormancy. Mix them with moist sand inside a sealed bag and leave them in the fridge for about 30 days. After that, they're ready to plant.

Once stratified, plant them just at the soil surface, no more than 5mm deep, in a sunny spot. Keeping them moist and warm (above 20°C for several consecutive days) is what gets them going. You can also start them indoors in small pots covered with a clear plastic container to create a greenhouse effect, which really helps germination.

Given that you're in Pennsylvania, you still have plenty of warm weeks ahead, so the timing isn't bad at all. Worth giving it a try!

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
